== Biography ==
'''NOTE: PARENTS ARE UNKNOWN'''
===Origins===
The origins of Richard Linton (aka Lynton) are unknown. He was likely born in England, probably about 1585-1590,<ref name=Holman>Holman, Mary Lovering. ''Ancestry of Colonel John Harrington Stevens and his wife Frances Helen Miller''. Concord, NH: privately printed at the Rumford Press, 1948, vol. 1, pp. 98-100 (Linton). [https://archive.org/details/ancestryofcolone01holm/page/98/mode/1up Archive.org].</ref> based on the estimated dates of birth of his daughters. The names of his parents are not known (see [[#Unknown Parents|research notes]], below).

===Marriage and Children===
Richard married a woman named [[Unknown-681309|Elizabeth]] _____,<ref>"U.S., New England Marriages Prior to 1700", database with images, Genealogical Publishing Co., Baltimore, MD. {{Ancestry Sharing|9073547|7b22746f6b656e223a22786634726f336d41456f7a6e7a7562306c45667944774c58374476464632794b447755634e59304d534c6b3d222c22746f6b656e5f76657273696f6e223a225632227d}} (free access) - {{Ancestry Record|3824|157947}}($): Elizabeth Linton marriage to Richard Linton in 1615 in England.</ref> who is named in deeds executed by Richard later in his life. No source is found for Elizabeth's last name at birth. 

If Elizabeth was Richard's only wife, the couple were probably married by 1611 in England. Elizabeth may be the mother of Richard's two children, or she could be a second wife, who he married in New England (see [[#Wife Elizabeth|research notes]]). Richard was the father of two daughters:
*[[Linton-797|Rachel]], born about 1612, married Henry Kibby and had one child;<ref name=Holman/> Rachel predeceased her father on 16 July 1657 in Dorchester,<ref>''A Report of the Record Commissioners of the City of Boston: Containing Dorchester Births, Marriages, and Deaths to the End of 1825''. Boston, MA: Rockwell and Churchill, city printers, 1890, p. 25. "Rachel Kebbey Deceased this Life the 16 : 5 : 1657". [https://www.google.com/books/edition/Records_Relating_to_the_Early_History_of/81IMAAAAYAAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=Rachel%20Kebbey%20Deceased%20this%20Life%20the%2016%20%3A%205%20%3A%201657&pg=PA25&printsec=frontcover Googe Books].</ref> and her daughter, Lydia, received what would have been Rachel's inheritance from Richard
*[[Linton-493|Anne]], born about 1614, died 6 February 1680[/1?], married Lawrence Waters<ref name=Holman/> and had several children<ref name=GM7>Robert Charles Anderson. ''The Great Migration, Immigrants to New England, 1634-1635'', Volume VII, T-Y. Boston MA: NEHGS, 2011, pp. 250-257. [https://www.americanancestors.org/DB496/i/0/250/0 AmericanAncestors.org]($)</ref>

===Life in New England===
At some point, Richard and both of his daughters emigrated to New England. The date[s] and ship[s] on which they arrived are unknown. The family may have traveled separately, as his daughters may have already been married by the time they emigrated. 

The first New England record for Richard is found in Massachusetts about 1638-1639: Watertown's first inventory of grants and possessions notes that Richard Linton owned a homestall of eight acres in the town.<ref>''Watertown Records'', Vol. 1. Watertown, MA: 1894, pp. 15, 30. [https://archive.org/details/watertownrecords01wate/page/n216/mode/1up Archive.org]</ref> See [[#Arrival in New England|research notes]] about a possible arrival in Massachusetts by 1630.

As early as 1643, Richard, his son-in-law Lawrence Waters, and John Ball moved their families to what was then called the Nashaway Plantation (now known as Lancaster, Massachusetts), where they had been tasked with "preparing the way for further settlement".<ref name=Nourse1884>Nourse, Henry S. ''Early Records of Lancaster, Massachusetts''. Lancaster: W. J. Coulter, 1884, pp. 37-41, 248, 252, 322 (death). [https://archive.org/details/earlyrecordsofla1643lanc/page/252/mode/1up Archive.org].</ref><ref name=HTL>Marvin, Abijah. ''History of the town of Lancaster, Massachusetts''. Lancaster: 1879, pp. 38-46. [https://archive.org/details/historyoftownofl00marv/page/38/mode/1up Archive.org].</ref>  In September 1645, Richard deeded his house and lot in Watertown to Robert Sanderson.<ref name=GM7/><ref name=Nourse1884/> By 1647, John Ball had left Lancaster and [[Prescott-34|John Prescott]] had set up permanent residence there along with Richard and Lawrence Waters. By 1653, there were nine families settled in Nashaway and the general court was petitioned for "Lancaster" to be incorporated as a town. The town of Lancaster was established in May 1653.<ref name=HTL/> Richard was named in 1654 divisions of land and meadows.<ref name=Nourse1884/> 

Richard disposed of much of his land by deed of gift before he died. On 13 March 1659[/60?], Richard Linton "of Lanchaster", deeded to "my daughter Ann Waters the wife of Laurance Waters of the same town" 15 acres of land in Lancaster. The deed was recorded on 6 October 1674,<ref name=GM7/> probably after the death of Richard's wife, Elizabeth.<ref name=Holman/> In another deed, dated the "7th of the 11th mo. 1662" (7 January 1662/3), Richard gave a great deal of property to his granddaughter Lydia Bennett and her husband George. The deed instructed that on their deaths, all of the property was to go to their son John. It went on to say that if John Bennett died without heirs, the property should go to any of John's living siblings [there were none], otherwise the property should go to Richard's daughter Anne, wife of Lawrence Waters, and their heirs (Middlesex Probate #14103).<ref name=Holman/>

===Death and Probate===
Richard died 30 March 1665 in Lancaster: "Richard Linton died 30. 1 mo. 1665".<ref name=Nourse1884/><ref>"Massachusetts, Town Clerk, Vital and Town Records, 1626-2001," database with images. [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:FC9N-848 FamilySearch.org]: Richard Linton, 30 May 1665; Death, Lanchaster, Massachusetts, FHL microfilm 892,249 </ref> His wife, Elizabeth, survived him.<ref name=Nourse1884/>

Richard probably did not leave a will as he had previously disposed of his lands by deeds of gift. Administration of his estate was granted to "ye selectmen of Lanchaster and Jeremiah Rogers in ye behalf and for ye use of the widow". Jeremiah Rogers filed an inventory on 20 June 1665 which included a few personal items and some lands.<ref name=Holman/><ref name=Nourse1884/><ref>Rodgers, R.H. ''Middlesex County in the Colony of the Massachusetts Bay in New England: Records of Probate and Administration, March 1660/61-December 1670''. Boston: NEHGS, 2001, p. 174. Not available online</ref> NOTE: Searched for Middlesex Probate #14103  and can't find it online.

Elizabeth's date and place of death are unknown. It is thought that she may have died by 1674, when Anne and Lawrence Waters filed the deed of gift from Richard.<ref name=Holman/>

==Research Notes==
===Unknown Parents===
The only sources for Richard's only sometimes listed parents ([[Linton-949|Richard Lindon/Linton]] and [[Fox-3610|Joan Fox]]) have been detached. 
 They come from unsourced online trees and a "Pedigree Resource File".<ref>The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, "Pedigree Resource File," database. [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/2:2:S59V-V1R FamilySearch.org]: entry for Richard LINTON</ref> These sources are not considered reliable. Robert Charles Anderson states that Richard's origins are unknown. No primary sources for his origins have been found. Additionally, there is no known family connection to Somerset, England (a location found in several unsourced online trees).

===Wife Elizabeth===
The profile of [[Hayward-276|Elizabeth Hayward-276]] has been detached as Richard's wife until a reliable source can be found to connect them.
 
There is no source for the following information that was previously included in the biography above: 
:"Before 1612, in Somerset, Richard married Elizabeth ''Hayward'', daughter of William Haward (born 1550) and Margery (?nee) Hayward, born 1552. Elizabeth was born about 1591, and had an elder brother John Will Hayward (1583-1639)".
 
Richard had only one known wife, Elizabeth _____ (last name unknown), who may or may not be the mother of his children (Holman believes Elizabeth may have been a second wife).<ref name=Holman/>

===Arrival in New England===
A "Richard Lynton" was recorded in a 28 September 1630 Massachusetts Bay inquiry about the manslaughter death of Austin Bratcher in Medford, Massachusetts. This Richard was listed as a person who had seen the body, but it was noted that he was absent at the time of the inquiry.<ref>Nathaniel B. Shurtleff, ed. ''Records of the Governor and Company of the Massachusetts Bay in New England'', Vol. 1 of 5. Boston: W. White, 1853, p. 78. [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=uma.ark:/13960/t0gt5x713&seq=102 HathiTrust.org].</ref> Many believe that the Richard in the 1630 list is the same man who was in Watertown in 1638 and in Lancaster, Massachusetts about 1643. However, Anderson states that there is no evidence to believe that these are the same men, and he says that the Richard who was "absent" was likely a young transient plantation worker in 1630; whereas the Richard of this profile was "a mature man with a family" in 1630.<ref name=GMB>Robert Charles Anderson. ''The Great Migration Begins: Immigrants to New England 1620-1633'', Vol. II.  Boston: NEHGS, 1995, pp. 1188-1189. [https://www.americanancestors.org/DB393/i/12107/1188/0 AmericanAncestors.org]($)</ref>

===Great Migration Series===
*Great Migration Directory entry: Linton, Richard: Unknown; 1630; Massachusetts Bay [GMB 1188-89; WF 455-56].
*GMB Sketch: https://www.americanancestors.org/DB393/i/12107/1188/0 NOTE: This is a very brief entry that does not name any family or land transactions. It simply argues that the Richard of this profile was probably ''not'' the same Richard who was listed in Massachusetts Bay in 1630.
